Chokan Valikhanov (1835 to 1865) was a Kazakh scholar, explorer and Russian army officer, often called the father of modern Kazakh history and ethnography. A great-grandson of Ablai Khan of the Kazakh Khanate, he studied at the cadet school in Omsk and served the Russian governor of western Siberia.

In 1858 and 1859 he travelled to Kashgar disguised as a merchant, when the region under the Qing was closed to outsiders. His report on Kashgaria was prized in St Petersburg during the Great Game between Russia and Britain. Among the Kyrgyz he wrote down an episode of the Manas epic, the first part of it ever put on paper.

In Omsk he became a close friend of the exiled writer Fyodor Dostoevsky, and in St Petersburg he worked with the Russian Geographical Society. Ill with tuberculosis, he went back to the steppe and died at 29. Kazakhstan's Academy of Sciences bears his name.
